The wider paved shoulders will provide a wider area for the many buggies that travel this corridor. Center line rumble strips will also be added to warn drivers that they are deviating from their travel lanes into possible on-coming traffic and reduce the risk of head-on collisions. Other repair or incidental work being proposed with the project includes repairing or replacing sections of substandard beam guard to current standards. The beam guard needing adjustments or replacement are located throughout the project corridor at five box culvert or bridge crossings and three steeper sloped embankments. Several of the existing concrete culvert pipes and endwall sections throughout the corridor have experienced separation at the joints and will be repaired by relaying the separated pipe sections and installing new endwalls. The existing culverts will be cleaned and the ditches near the culvert ends will be cleaned within the existing right-of-way to clear brush, debris, and sediment to provide proper drainage. Concrete box culvert C-27-0012 located east of CTH T on the North Fork Buffalo River will have concrete surface repairs completed on the inside of the culvert. All proposed work will take place within the existing right-of-way. STH 22 will be closed from CTH QQ to CTH K for 5 days (Monday- Friday) to install the pipe. Signage at CTH QQ and CTH K will allow local traffic acess to businesses and residents. The eastbound approach (STH 105) is expected to operate at a LOS E during the PM peak period. Delay (35 seconds/vehicle) and queues (75-ft) are expected to remain minimal during this period. Left turning vehicles will cause mainline STH 35 traffic to slow/stop until gaps are available in the opposing direction. A Synchro traffic analysis was completed to represent flagging operations as closely as possible. It was found that queue lengths and delay increase during the AM and PM peak hours due to the flagging operations and drops to LOS E/F for all approaches. It was determined from a 48-hour coverage count (site # 160310) on STH 35 that the largest nighttime hourly traffic volume is approximately 75% less than the PM peak hour traffic volumes. USH 18 will remain open to traffic throughout the project. Lane closures can be maintained 24 hours a day, except during the lane closure restriction times or holidays and events where the roadway must be opened back up. This will be necessary to limit the amount of Special High Early Strength (SHES) concrete used on the project. SHES concrete has a much higher price and lower overall service life. All lane and ramp closures are subject to the approval of the Region traffic engineer. When the work zone is not active the traffic control drums must be placed completely within the closed lane to accommodate OSOW vehicles. Access to all businesses along and near the USH 18 corridor will be maintain. There are no schools directly within the project limits. Schools near the project area are located within the Village of Mount Horeb. No impacts to schools are anticipated. Northbound STH 78 will be detoured down to the USH 18/USH 151/CTH ID interchange while work along STH 78 is completed. Southbound STH 78 will remain open at all times. CTH ID interchange will require a detour for the two EB ramps for a structure closure on the bridge work. CTH JG will be closed while the wing wall, bearings and north abutment expansion joint are replaced at B-13-300 (CTH JG over USH 18). Interim liquidated damages will be accessed if the STH 78 and CTH ID detours or the CTH JG closure exceeds the maximum calendars days shown in the special provisions. The STH 78 and CTH ID detours will not be allowed to occur at the same time. Closure of CTH JG is not permitted while the STH 78 or CTH ID detours are in place. No impacts to businesses, schools, and everyday services are anticipated while these detours or closure are in place.

STH 32 has a 2017 AADT of 13,000. The WisDOT planning-level forecasts do not show any traffic growth at this location, so for the purpose of this analysis a 2% annual growth rate was used. Synchro 11 and SimTraffic traffic modeling software, using Highway Capacity Manual (HCM) 6th Edition methodology, was used to estimate traffic conditions during these closures. Single lane closures (reduced from 2-lanes to 1-lane) are permitted in each direction during overnight hours only (permitted closure times are identified in Section 6). The majority of work including pavement milling, base patching, and repaving operations will occur during the overnight hours when the lane closures are in place. Work not requiring lane closures may occur during daytime hours. See TMP ID 7551 for limited permitted daytime lane closure hours associated with the cable barrier work. Schedule/Sequencing of work and traffic control will be coordinated between the three tied let projects. Construction will include two general stages to avoid traffic control conflicts between the railroad bridge rehab and resurfacing projects (see description below). The cable barrier Segment 1 project is located within the resurfacing project limits and will be installed concurrently with the resurfacing work. Traffic control staging must be coordinated between these two projects. During overnight work, either separate work zones must be established for the cable barrier and resurfacing work with a minimum separation of 3 miles or a single work zone must be established encompassing both work activities that may not exceed 5 miles in length. Further, an inside lane closure for cable barrier work may not be preceded or followed by an outside lane closure for resurfacing work. The cable barrier Segment 2 limits are located more than 3 miles away from the CNW Railroad bridges (1067-01-85) and the resurfacing (1067-04-72) projects, allowing for separate work zone operations. However, the cable barrier Segment 2 is located in close proximity (less than 1 mile east) of a bridge re-decking/widening project along the County A overpass of I-94 (1067-02-72) which is scheduled to occur simultaneously in 2021. Overnight lane closures along I-94 are proposed with the County A overpass project. #### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

Access to traffic generators will be maintained throughout construction. The milling and paving operations along mainline STH 172 will be completed under traffic. Single lane closures will be permitted in both directions. A full closure will be required to complete the work along the single lane STH 172/IH 41 interchange ramps. Traffic will be detoured for the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 while the concrete pavement is being replaced. The detour will direct traffic along NB IH 41 to CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue). The work for the other single lane ramps will not have detours but lane closures will be allowed as specified in the lane closures.

#### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

The curb ramps at the STH 172 & Packerland Drive/CTH EB and the STH 172 & Babcock Road intersections will be replaced with the project. While the curb ramps are being replaced the associated Packerland Drive bike trail will be closed and appropriate signage will be in place (see attached Traffic Control Plan). The public will be informed of the planned work and closure of the path through public involvement meetings, press releases/media alerts, the project website, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website.

#### **Describe how impacts to airports will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Airport personnel will be notified of the project and will be kept informed of changes in traffic control during construction by construction personnel. Lane closures will only be allowed during the times specified in the special provisions. The public will be informed of the planned work and lane closures through public involvement meetings, press releases/media alerts, the project website, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

IH 41 and CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue) traffic will be impacted by the project. Traffic along the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 will be detoured along NB IH 41 to CTH VK while the concrete pavement along the ramp is being replaced. The detour route will be signed per the traffic control plans.

#### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

No.

#### **List holidays or major special events that occur during the project:**

| Holiday/Special Event           | Begin Date | End Date   |
|---------------------------------|------------|------------|
| Memorial Day 2023               | 05/26/2023 | 05/30/2023 |
| Independence Day 2023           | 06/30/2023 | 07/05/2023 |
| Labor Day 2023                  | 09/01/2023 | 09/05/2023 |
| Lambeau Field Events of 30,000+ | 04/01/2023 | 11/01/2023 |

#### **How will traffic disruptions be minimized during listed events and holidays?**

The special provisions will include language indicating, "Do not perform work on, nor haul materials of any kind along or across any portion of the highway carrying STH 172 traffic and entirely clear the traveled way and shoulders of such portions of the highway of equipment, barricades, signs, lights, and any other material that might impede the free flow of traffic during the events listed above".

--- End of Section 5 ---
